title: Kuldeep Yadav's Career-Best Ten-For Powers Yorkshire to Innings Win Over Essex
excerpt: The India wrist-spinner's 10 for 120 — his first ten-wicket haul in first-class cricket — sank Essex twice at Headingley and all but sealed Yorkshire's Division One survival.
body:
• India left-arm wrist-spinner Kuldeep Yadav took career-best first-class match figures of 10 for 120 — 4 for 70 and 6 for 50 — as Yorkshire beat Essex by an innings and 106 runs inside three days at Headingley.
  • Essex were bowled out for 171 and then 113 after being asked to follow on, chasing Yorkshire's 390 built on Dom Bess's unbeaten 80.
  • The 22-point haul all but secures Yorkshire's Division One status for next season with two games to go, while a sixth defeat deepens Essex's relegation worries.
  • Kuldeep named his dismissal of Essex captain Tom Westley — a sharp turner that flattened middle stump — as his "ball of the day."

Kuldeep Yadav produced the finest first-class bowling performance of his career, claiming ten wickets in the match as Yorkshire demolished Essex by an innings and 106 runs at Headingley on Thursday. The three-day victory in the Rothesay County Championship's 57th match all but guaranteed Yorkshire's place in Division One next summer.

The India wrist-spinner finished with career-best match figures of 10 for 120: 4 for 70 from 20 overs in the first innings and 6 for 50 from 16 in the second. It was his first ten-wicket haul in first-class cricket, and it came with Yorkshire fighting to secure their top-flight future.

Context & Background

Yorkshire laid the platform before Kuldeep took over. Dom Bess's unbeaten 80 anchored a first-innings 390, with Adam Lyth (62), Matthew Revis (61), and William Luxton (50) all contributing; Matt Critchley was Essex's best bowler with 5 for 85. In reply, Essex crumbled to 171 — Kuldeep and Bess (3 for 36) and George Hill (3 for 12) doing the damage — and were asked to follow on. They collapsed again for 113, with Kuldeep taking six of the ten wickets.

County stints have become an important proving ground for Indian spinners, offering experience on English pitches that rarely assist turn. Kuldeep, playing for Yorkshire, showed quality needs no boundary: his dismissal of Essex captain Tom Westley in the first innings saw the ball pitch well outside off stump, turn sharply, and flatten middle stump — a delivery some reports described as reminiscent of the sport's most famous turning balls.

Impact & Analysis

The scorecard tells only part of the story. In the second innings, Kuldeep twice came within a wicket of a hat-trick, dismissing Charles Allison and Matt Critchley with consecutive deliveries at Headingley, while George Hill's seam movement did the early damage up top. Together, Kuldeep and Hill took the match apart in three days — a ruthless finish to a fixture Yorkshire simply could not afford to lose.

"I started, and my first couple of balls were really good, and then I tried to mix it up with my variations. I thought the ball which I bowled to Walter was a very good one, slid on and a bit quicker through the air. Then Westley's ball was my ball of the day."

— Kuldeep Yadav, speaking to Yorkshire media

The result was Yorkshire's fourth win in 12 matches. Combined with a 22-point haul, it opened significant breathing space above the bottom two places with two games remaining. For Essex, a sixth defeat leaves them looking over their shoulders at the wrong end of the table, with title-chasing Warwickshire visiting Chelmsford next week — exactly the fixture a relegation-threatened side does not want.

Diaspora Angle

For Indian cricket fans in England, Kuldeep's masterclass was a rare treat: an Indian spinner winning a county match almost single-handedly, in front of a Headingley crowd, on pitches where wrist-spin rarely rules. His county spell has been closely followed back home too, as Indian fans track every Indian player's form in English conditions ahead of future tours.

What's Next

Yorkshire now control their own destiny with two matches to play, while Essex must find a way to stop the slide before the season's end. For Kuldeep, a career-best ten-for on English soil strengthens the case for him as an overseas player and a match-winner in any conditions — and gives Indian supporters one more reason to keep an eye on the County Championship's closing weeks.
